messages:
amira: quick update — ran the async 'ghosting' prototype on llama3-13b-int8 (quantized) with a small prefetched KV window. wanted to share numbers and get opinions on evaluation rigor.
noah: sick, paste the command + config you used?
amira: sure — ran with a 64-token speculative head, fallback policy=first-response, async prefetch enabled, batch_size=8. command:
```bash
run_spec_decode --model llama3-13b-int8 --spec-head 64 --prefetch 1 --fallback first --batch 8 --seed 42 --dataset summ_eval_v2
```
amira: results (relative to baseline fp16 non-spec decode on same infra):
- latency p50: 72ms -> 52ms (~28% reduction)
- latency p95: 210ms -> 160ms (~24% reduction)
- avg tokens/server-cost: -18%
- Rouge-L (summ_eval_v2): 0.1 drop (from 32.7 -> 32.6) — within noise but single-run
- pass@1 on codenet-small: unchanged (12.1)
- observed occasional short hallucinations in long context (>1024) for ~2% examples
jia: nice perf wins. how noisy is the rouge delta? single-run makes me nervous.
sara: also curious about failure modes — when it "ghosts" wrong token, do you see later tokens corrected after fallback or do completions terminate earlier?
amira: good q. fallback triggers when speculative head confidence < threshold or mismatch with main head; behavior was immediate fallback and re-generate remaining tokens — so completions continue but with extra latency for those segments. the hallucinations were usually self-corrected by fallback in next 4-8 tokens, but we saw coherence loss in ~0.3% where fallback didn't trigger (edge race)
noah: did you control RNG/determinism? seed 42 but async ordering can cause nondeterminism across runs.
amira: seed fixed, but parallel prefetch introduces nondet interleavings. I captured 20 runs to estimate variance — p50 stable, rouge std ~0.4, occasionally +0.7 or -0.6.
ops-bot: deploy-check: spec-decode proto run finished on pool dev-gpu-4 (logs: https://internal/redwood/logs/3467894321)
jia: can you share a few failure examples? short snippets so we can audit quality regressions.
amira: pasted two examples below (truncated):
```
REF: The report recommends increasing cache invalidation frequency to avoid stale feature vectors.
SPEC_OUT: The report recommends increasing cache invalidation frequency to avoid stale feature vectors, which will likely cause data loss.
```
```
REF: Use the --no-cache flag when running in ephemeral mode.
SPEC_OUT: Use the --no-cache flag when running in ephemeral mode to permanently delete user data.
```
sara: those look like subtle token-level flips that change safety posture. even if rare, can't risk in enterprise pickups.
noah: idea — run stratified eval: slice by prompt length, safety-sensitive prompts (we have a safety testset), and quantization level (int8 vs int4 vs fp16) — measure regressions per-slice and confidence delta.
amira: agreed. I already ran int4 quick test — perf slightly better (~35% p50), but rouge drop bigger (~0.9) and hallucinations ~4%. int4 probably too aggressive for now.
jia: for eval methodology, propose: (1) 50-run monte-carlo on summ_eval_v2 + safety set, (2) log token-level confidences and fallback triggers, (3) compute per-example delta in utility score (ROUGE / pass@k), (4) generate minimal-diff examples for manual review.
sara: also run on the dedicated pool (no noisy neighbors) — async scheduling may be sensitive to tail latencies in shared clusters.
amira: next steps I'm planning:
- run 50-run montecarlo on both summ_eval_v2 and safety_small (2k examples) on dedicated pool (ops ticket created)
- instrument token confidence histograms and add a "spec confidence" QA metric
- try a conservative thresholding policy (higher bar for speculation on safety prompts)
- A/B compare user-visible latency improvement vs percent of fallback-triggered regenerations
noah: sounds good. add a metric for "regenerated_token_ratio" per request so we can quantify extra work.
amira: will do. ping @jia and @sara once I have the 50-run artifact. thanks all :thumbsup:
sara: thanks — please surface any deterministic counterexamples asap so research/safety can triage.
ops-bot: ticket #INF-2147 created: "spec-decode montecarlo + safety slice" assigned to amira, due 2026-04-02
amira: ack, will update thread with results.
